headline: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra Produces Proof of 50-Year-Old Cycle Double Cover Conjecture
raw_snippet: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra produced a proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture, a graph theory problem posed independently by George Szekeres (1973) and Paul Seymour (1979), using 64 parallel subagents in under one hour. The proof was published as a PDF on OpenAI's CDN. Graph theorists are expected to spend weeks stress-testing the argument; the proof has not yet been peer-reviewed.
curator_notes: Capability milestone: 50-year-old math conjecture proved (pending peer review)

headline: OpenAI Publishes 'Separating Signal from Noise in Coding Evaluations,' Retracts SWE-Bench Pro Recommendation
raw_snippet: OpenAI published a research paper on July 8 detailing a comprehensive audit of SWE-Bench Pro. The team found approximately 30% of the benchmark's 731 tasks are broken. OpenAI stated it 'no longer believes SWE-Bench Pro reliably measures frontier coding capability' and retracted its earlier recommendation to adopt it as a leading evaluation. Five independent software engineers cross-validated the findings.

headline: OpenAI Researcher Says GPT-5.6 Is Better at AI Research Than Most Human Interns
raw_snippet: Senior OpenAI researcher Noam Brown said at ICML in Seoul that he would choose GPT-5.6 over a human research intern for most tasks. CEO Sam Altman had previously said OpenAI would have an automated AI research intern by September 2026. Another researcher, Yash Pande, suggested one way to measure progress would be changes in the number of AI chips researchers allocate to the AI coding tool Codex for research tasks.

headline: OpenAI Deprecates Atlas Browser, Shifts Agentic Browsing to Chrome Extension and Desktop App
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced on July 9 that Atlas, its AI-powered browser launched in October 2025, will be deprecated and stop working on August 9, 2026. The company is folding Atlas's agentic browsing features into the ChatGPT desktop app and a new Google Chrome extension. OpenAI concluded that 'the browser is a feature, not the destination.' Browser data including bookmarks and history will not transfer automatically.
curator_notes: Product sunset: Atlas browser killed after 9 months, features folded into main app

headline: Microsoft Replaces OpenAI and Anthropic Models with Own MAI AI in Excel and Outlook
raw_snippet: Microsoft is replacing OpenAI and Anthropic models with its internally built MAI models in Excel and Outlook, with tens of thousands of AI prompts being completed weekly by MAI. AI model chief Mustafa Suleyman said the company was trying to 'reduce and ultimately eliminate' Anthropic spending by using more MAI models. OpenAI and Anthropic still handle most Copilot traffic, but Microsoft is steadily reducing its dependence.

headline: OpenAI Safety Chief Johannes Heidecke to Leave After Reorganization
raw_snippet: Johannes Heidecke, OpenAI's head of safety, announced his departure on July 11 following a company reorganization that merges safety and research teams. He will leave by July 24. Safety teams will now report to VP of research Mia Glaese, with Saachi Jain as interim head of safety systems. Heidecke is the sixth senior safety-leader exit since May 2024.
